items.prompt: A finite sample has finite computed variance. What does this prove about population variance?

options.text: It proves the population variance is finite
options.why: Rare unobserved tail events can change population moments.

options.text: It proves the distribution is normal
options.why: Many nonnormal finite samples have finite arithmetic variance.

options.text: It proves no larger observations are possible
options.why: The sample maximum does not establish the population support.

options.text: It does not establish population variance
options.why: Moment existence is a property of the full model/distribution.

items.explanation: Finite-sample arithmetic and infinite-population convergence are different claims.
